en: I bow at the two feet of Vajrasattva; for the sake of the accomplishment of practitioners, this *Balimālikā* is being written.
By the very offering of this bali, all these beings are gratified; the entire cycle of protection and so forth becomes auspicious, followed by awakening.
Therefore, the true nature of the bali offering for my sake should be understood by those esteemed by the virtuous.

Pacification, enrichment, subjugation, and likewise malevolent rites—these are accomplished merely by means of the offering of oblations; there is no doubt in this matter. This *Balimālikā*, composed by Māyāsumati-siṃha, shines like a wish-fulfilling gem (*cintāmaṇi*) always worn around the neck of practitioners of mantra.

Here, one should offer the *bali* with the verses stated in the *Subāhutantra*: "With baskets, carts, loads, heaps, and likewise with handfuls; there, in one place, the *bali*, the *argha*, and the water for scent and so forth—this very [offering] belongs to the Asuras, Sarvabhujas, Ganasiddhas, Tārkṣyas, Suparṇas, and Kaṭapūtanas."
And whatever divine beings of the Gandharva, Siddha,
and Agra-haja classes who dwell upon the surface of the earth—
to each of them I make this request, kneeling on one knee with palms joined in reverence: together with their sons, wives, servants, and retinues.

Having heard this, let those beings who dwell here for the sake of showing favor come forth; those who reside upon my back, those among the Nandana groves and the abodes of the gods and others, those who are in the intermediate spaces of that mountain, all those who dwell among the nāgas, those at all rivers and confluences,
those who have made their paths in the repositories of jewels, and those in the ponds, lakes, and lotus-pools.
Those who dwell in wells, in thunderbolts, and in waterfalls; those who are in village hamlets and in divine groves, or in empty houses and temples;

those who are in monasteries, shrines, dwellings, hermitages, and in oil-presses, halls, and elephant stables; those who are in the variegated palaces of mountain lords, on carriage-roads, in streets, and at crossroads; and those who are under solitary trees or on great highways.
In great cremation grounds and in great forests.
And those who dwell in the terrible great forests, inhabited by lions and bears;

Those who have made their abodes in the divine islands, and those who dwell upon Mount Meru or in the cremation grounds— may they, joyful and well-pleased, accept with devotion this offspring, perfumes, garlands, incense, offerings, and the increasing light of lamps; may they partake of, enjoy, and drink this and this.
May they accept this offering of the fruit of karma! Mahābali!
(1) Oṃ vajrayoginī hrīḥ | tu ña | khaḥ pheṃ ña aṃ ña | grant me the accomplishment of my mind; accept, accept the offering! hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā!
A white offering for the night of the sky.
(2) Oṃ! Piśāciparṇaśavari, destroyer of all forests, pacifier of all diseases, destroyer of all fears, accept this offering, accept it! Kha kha khāhi!
Eat! Kill all evil ones, kill! Bind, bind! Strike, strike! Burn, burn! Cook, cook! Slay, slay! Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā! This is the *parṇaśavarī* offering.
(3) Oṃ, you who abide by the command of Mahākāla, the devourer of crows; you who are the western time, this...
For those who revile the Three Jewels: if you fulfill your vow, then take this offering, take it!
Kha kha! Khāhi khāhi! Subdue, subdue all wicked beings! Seize, seize! Bind, bind! Strike, strike! Burn, burn! Cook, cook! With a single [utterance], slay, slay the wretched one! Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ!
Svāhā! The offering to Mahākāla. (4) Oṃ āḥ hūṃ hoḥ! To Uṣṇīṣa, Sumbharāja, Yamāntaka, Prajñāntaka, Padmāntaka, Vighnāntaka, Acala, Ḍākkirāja, Nīladaṇḍa, and Mahābala: [svāhā].
To you and your retinues, we offer this bali, perfume, flowers, incense, lamp, and unbroken rice.
May you come with your retinues and quickly accept and consume this bali. Jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ!
Having been satisfied, grant peace, nourishment, protection, defense, and concealment to me and all sentient beings.
HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ PAHṬ VAJRADHARA ĀJÑĀPAYATI SVĀHĀ. This is the offering for the ten wrathful deities.
OṂ ĀḤ HŪṂ HOḤ! To those residing here, to the guardians of the fields (kṣetrapāla), and to others as well—we offer this fragrance, flowers, incense, lamps, and unbroken grains.

May they, together with their retinues and modes of movement, swiftly accept this offering, eat it, and drink it: *jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ*. Being satisfied, may they grant peace, nourishment, protection, defense, and concealment for me and all sentient beings:
*hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ*. Vajradhara commands: *svāhā*. This is the *kṣetrapāla* offering.

(6) Oṃ, homage to the Tathāgata Surūpa, the Arhat, the perfectly awakened one. It is as follows: Oṃ suru suru, prasuru prasuru, tara tara, bhara bhara, sambhara sambhara, santarpaya santarpaya, [for] all pretas, svāhā! May those who move away, those who do not move away, and those who wander about depart!
I give this food to the *preta*s dwelling in all world-systems; this is the *bali* offering for the *preta*s.

(7) Oṃ! To those situated in the ten directions, to those present here—this *bali* is offered to the gods, *garuḍas*, *kinnaras*, *mahoragas*, *bhūtas*, *pretas*, *piśācas*, *unmādas*, *apasmāras*, *ostārakas*, and so forth.
We offer these flowers, incense, lamps, perfumes, and food offerings; having accepted them, may they become partakers of happiness and well-being. May they also render this place free from harm.
Through the empowerment of all the Buddhas: Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ. Having consumed this mass of nectar, [may there be well-being] for me and for all beings.

And may they grant peace, well-being, and *svāhā*. This is the offering for all spirits (*sarvabhautika-bali*) for the members of the assembly. (8) May the goddess Indrāṇī, together with the hosts of Vajrin and the Bhūtas, accept this distinguished offering; as well as Agni, Yama, Nairṛti, the Lord of Beings (Bhūpati), and the Lord of Waters (Apāmpati).
Vāyu and Dhana-pati; Īśāna and Bhūtādhipati; the gods above, and the Moon, Sun, and Pitāmaha;

all the gods on earth together with the hosts of Nāgas, Dharas, and Guhyakas—let them, each in their own respective well-established regions, accept this single announcement of our resolve with satisfaction. May they be auspicious.

Together with their wives, sons, friends, and kinsmen, may they partake of, smell, and drink this flower, offering, incense, and oblation; and may they enjoy this and that fruit of their actions. The Offering to the Guardians of the Directions:
(9) Oṃ pheṃ hrīṃ hū jaḥ, [accept] the offering, the red flowers, and the king of all *kāmarāja* siddhas.

Grant [this] to me! Likewise, reduce these thought-creations to ashes! Make the enemies who have gone to the seven netherworlds as the soles of my feet! Bring peace to all people! Phaṭ svāhā! This is the *kāmarāja-bali*. (10) Oṃ hrīḥ! Come, come, Ekajaṭī, together with Mamo and Panyutā! Bring peace!

Bestow nourishment! O Great Lord of Yakṣas, take this offering, take it, take it! Drink, drink! Draw forth the spells of others, draw them forth! Truṭa truṭa! Muṭa muṭa! Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā! This is the offering to Ugratārā.
(11) Oṃ āḥ hrīṃ hrīṃ Kurukulle! You who bring all sentient beings under your power, you who cause all fears to be dispelled! We offer this bali, fragrance, flower, incense, lamp, and unbroken grain.
May all the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, and others, enjoy this according to their desire.
Eat! Drink! Smell! Grant us, each of us, success! Oṃ āḥ hrīṃ hrīṃ phaṭ svāhā! This is the bali offering for Kurukullā.
(12) Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the glorious Caṇḍamahāroṣaṇa!

To the one who destroys the entire host of Māra for the sake of the armies of gods, asuras, and humans; to the one with the body of *atasī* flowers; to the one who has made Akṣobhya his crest-ornament:
accept this offering, accept it! Ward off, ward off all my obstacles and the four Māras!
Terrify, terrify! Confound, confound! Cut, cut! Pierce, pierce!

Destroy! Destroy! Torment! Torment! Dry up! Dry up! Cut! Cut! Split! Split! Reduce to ashes all wicked beings who harbor hostile intentions toward me! HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ! This is the offering for Caṇḍamahāroṣaṇa.
(13) OṂ JAMBHALA, to Jalendra, the possessor of great wealth!
To the Great Yakṣa General: accept, accept this offering of the five nectars! Kha kha! Khāhi khāhi! Remember your pledge! Jaḥ jaḥ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā! This is the Jambhala offering.
[5] (14) Oṃ, to the one with the red crown, the red face, and the red body...

To the one with blood-red arms, to the one adorned with garlands of blood-red necklaces, to the one mounted upon a red chariot, to the one with a red face, to the one decorated with red ornaments—accept this offering, accept it! Remove all my obstacles, remove them! Ward off the four Māras, ward them off! Terrify them, terrify them! Confound them, confound them! Cut them down, cut them down!

Vinda vinda! Nāśaya nāśaya! Śoṣaya śoṣaya! Cinda cinda! Bheda bheda! Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā! One should cause it to circulate by means of the subsequent portion: *indrāya namaḥ hrīḥ*, *yamāya namaḥ strīḥ*, *varuṇāya namaḥ vi*, *kuverāya namaḥ kri*, *agnaye namaḥ ta*, *īśvarāya namaḥ ā*.

Homage to Nairṛti, *namaḥ*; homage to Navāyu, *namaḥ*; homage to Naṅgula, *namaḥ* hūṃ; homage to Arka, *namaḥ* hūṃ; homage to Brahmamaṇi, *namaḥ* phaṭ; homage to Vasudhārā, *namaḥ* phaṭ; homage to Avilamacitriṇī, *namaḥ* svāhā;
homage to all beings (*sarvabhūtebhyaḥ*), *namaḥ* svāhā. Ha hā hi hu hū hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā. This is the bali offering to Raktayamāri.

(15) Oṃ Tāriṇī, remover of all suffering and fear, slayer of the four Māras, O Vāriṇī, crusher of all calamities caused by gods, asuras, humans, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and others; destroyer of bhūtas, pretas, yakṣas, ḍākinīs, and the like; annihilator of the three—poisons, spells, and tantras.
O Blessed One, Durgatpariṇī, come, come! Accept, accept this offering! Slay, slay all my enemies! Eat, eat them! Burn, burn all fetters, diseases, and seizing spirits!
Shatter, shatter! Split, split! Burst, burst! Grant me all accomplishments!

Bestow peace, nourishment, and protection upon me! Cut down, cut down! Shatter, shatter! Destroy, destroy! Agitate, agitate! Paralyze, paralyze! all strife, quarrels, and planetary afflictions (*graha*)! Sever those who manifest disputes and obstacles! Hrīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ! Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ! Āḥ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā! This is the *bali* offering for Durgottārā.

(16) Oṃ vajrāralli hoḥ! O Vajra-ḍākinīs, you are the pledge; appear, hoḥ! With the vajra-añjali gesture, with the hands opened upwards, one should offer the bali to the practitioner: Oṃ kha kha! Khāhi khāhi! [All] yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, unmādas, apasmāras, ḍākas, ḍākinīs, and so forth—this...

May they accept the offering, protect my commitment, and grant me all accomplishments exactly as desired. Eat! Consume! Drink! Smell! Do not transgress against me in every way. Be assistants for the sake of attaining true happiness and prosperity. HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ.
The *Cakrasaṃvara* Bali offering:
(17) Oṃ, homage to the Blessed Lady, the Red One with Three Eyes, the Great Fierce Vajrapāṇi! Contract, contract all the limbs of all my enemies!

Break, break! Crush, crush! O Blessed One, Vajraśrīṅkhalā! O Vajrapāṇi, bind the necks [of the enemies]! Draw them in, draw them in! Bind their eyes! Bind their heads! Tear apart all their limbs! Kill, kill! Accept, accept the flower, incense, perfume, and the offering! Svāhā! This is the offering to Vajraśrīṅkhalā.

(18) Oṃ Vajravārāhī, eat this bali, kha kha! Khāhi khāhi! May all yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, apasmāras, ḍākas, ḍākinīs, and so forth, accept this bali! Protect the samaya; enjoy, eat, drink, and smell it according to your own desire and as you wish.

Do not transgress me in any way; O true bliss, be my companions for the sake of increase! HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ. This is the *bali* offering to Vajravārāhī. (19) Homage to the Blessed Lady Vajratārā, the accomplisher of all siddhis.
O remover of all fears, accept, accept this offering and the five nectars! Kha kha! Khāhi khāhi!

For my sake, paralyze, paralyze all the wicked and malicious ones! For delusion, for delusion! For salutation, for salutation! Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ! O Vajratārā who paralyzes all the wicked, svāhā!
The *Bali* offering for Vajratāta-Āra.
(20) Homage to all Buddhas! Homage to all Dharmas! Homage to all Saṅghas! Oṃ Sitātapatra! Oṃ Vimala! Oṃ Śaṃkara! Oṃ!
O Pratyaṅgiravajra, Uṣṇīṣacakravartin! Sever, sever, pierce, pierce all those root-rites of binding, striking, or pinning with any kind of yantra performed by anyone on my behalf! Cira cira! Giri!
Giri mara mara hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ. This is the *uṣṇīṣa*-cakravartin offering. Oṃ āḥ.

It encompasses the convergence of the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), abiding in every single moment within the succession of mandalas consisting of atoms from the infinite clouds and oceans of space that pervade the world-systems of the ten directions throughout all three times.

Equal to the space-element, they are like the sky in their extension through the infinite arrays of world-systems throughout the ten directions and the worlds of the three times; such are all the world-protectors and all sentient beings, namely:
Vajrāyudha, Vajrakāla, Nāgavajra, Vajrabhirava, Vajranala, and Vajramusala.

Vajranīla, Vajrakrodha, Vajramauna, Vajramāyā, Vajraśauṇḍa, Vajrasrabha, Vajrakrodha, Vemacitri, and Pṛthivīdevatā, together with your retinues: accept this offering of bali, flowers, incense, lamps, perfumes, food offerings, and the like; enjoy this presentation of bali, and [subdue] all my obstacles, impediments, and all malevolent beings.

O humans, crush them! Paralyze them! Rejoice! Destroy them! For the sake of the increase of my great happiness—my gold, silver, wealth, grain, life-span, youth, health, and pleasures—bring them all forth to me as aids until I reach the seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa). Grant me peace, nourishment, and protection! Oṃ!

Āḥ Mañjuvajra maṃ hūṃ svāhā. This is the bali offering for Mañjuvajra Vāgiśvara. (22) Oṃ ehy ehi, Blessed One, Vajrayoginī, fulfiller of all desires, Blessed One, granter of boons; homage to you, homage to you! Again and again, homage to you!

O Mother of the Goddesses, grant me your grace! Accept this offering, accept it! Oṃ vajravairocanīye svāhā! This is the *vajrayoginī-bali* consisting of one hundred and fifty syllables, as taught in the *Acalakalpa*. [8] (23) Oṃ, remember the commitment (*samaya*) of all the Tathāgatas! Hūṃ hūṃ pheṃ!
*Phreṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā*. This is the *rakṣāgagana-kṣepa-bali*.
(24) *Oṃ vajraḍākini idaṃ baliṃ hrī hrī ha haiṃ haṃ hiḥ phaṭ mama sarvasattvānāṃ ca śāntiṃ kuru svāhā*. On the eighth and fourteenth days of the lunar month, at the time of Yama...
The *bali* offering for Vajralokinī according to the sequence of Śabarapāda:
(25) Oṃ vajraḍākinī, accept this *bali*, accept it! Ha ha ha haḥ | Kha kha kha kha | Ya ya ya ya | A a a aḥ | Grant me accomplishment, hūṃ phaṭ!

Phaṭ! This is the bali offering for the glorious Advayavajrapāda, the Vajrayoginī. Oṃ! To the one who burns away evil intellect, who possesses the luster of a moonstone gem, whose hands are occupied with a sword and a book, the excellent Mañjuvajra!

(26) Oṃ a-ra-pa-ca-na-ya! To the one skilled in incinerating ignorance! To the one with the radiance of a moon-gem! To the one whose hands are busy with a sword and a volume! To the one with a beautiful forest! Mañjuvanīvara!

O bestower of the accomplishment of Mañjubuddhi, accept this offering—scent, flower, incense, lamp, honey, and sugar, etc. Accept! Accept! Kha kha! Khādi khādi! Grant me peace, nourishment, protection, defense, and concealment! Oṃ āḥ dhīḥ hūṃ svāhā! This is the *ara-pa-ca-na* offering.

(27) Oṃ mahāśrīye trī hūṃ hrīḥ oṃ! Accept this offering, accept it! For the sake of the three worlds and the cycle of existence, tear asunder poverty! Smash, smash all the wicked and the extremely malevolent! Come, come! O Blessed One, grant me a treasure-trove! Svāhā! This is the Mahāśrītārā bali-offering.

(28) Oṃ, O Blessed One, O Dispeller of the Eight Great Fears, who brings about peace, prosperity, and vision, O Destroyer of yantras, mantras, poisons, and powders, O Great Mistress of Yoga! Grant protection for me and for all sentient beings;
deliver us, deliver us from the eight great and terrible fears! O You of divine form, O Gentle-faced One!
Take this offering, take it! Kha kha! Eat, eat! Svāhā! This is the *bali* offering for protection from the eight great fears.
(29) Oṃ, Blessed One, homage to you, the Praśastā! Oṃ, to the *ḍākinī* of all Buddhas!
O Vajravairocanī, take this offering, take it! Kha kha! Khāhi khāhi!

Reduce to ashes those who harbor hostile intentions toward me! Make my enemies, even those dwelling in the seven netherworlds, as if under the soles of my feet! Grant me everywhere peace, nourishment, protection, defense, and concealment! Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā!
The Bali offering for the Vajrayoginī of the Three Bodies.
(30) Oṃ, you who possess the vajra authority over all phenomena, O Great Kāla of the Vajra Command, come to the place of the palm-clap! Ha hūṃ hīṃ kṣiṃ, this—
Accept the offering, accept! Kha kha! Eat, eat! O tamer of all wicked beings!
Ha hā hi hī hu hū he hai ho hau haṃ haḥ phaṭ svāhā! Oṃ, this is the offering for Vajramahākāla.
(31) Oṃ Mahāpratyamgira, you who bring peace to all that is auspicious! Asīti.
O performer of a hundred thousand yogas, accept, accept this offering, perfume, flower, incense, and lamp!
Whatever mechanical device, mantra, tantra, poison, powder, or application has been done or caused to be done against me—destroy all that!
Destroy it! Burn it! Burn it! Cook it! Cook it! Grind it! Grind it! Roar! Roar! Threaten! Threaten!
May it fall upon his very head, svāhā! This is the Mahāpratyaṅgirā offering.
(32) Oṃ, Mahāpratisarā, Mahāsāhasrapramardanī, Mahāmāyūrī, Mahāśītavatī, Mahāmantrānusāriṇī, and the Buddhis, those Great-Souled Ones, and the Goddesses of Knowledge.

Mahābali; Māmakī and Bhṛkuṭī; Tārā, Āvītā, Kuśī, Vajraśrī, Śṛṅkhalā, and likewise Śvetā; Mahākālī and her messengers (dūtīs), as well as the messengers of the Vajra (vajradūtīs) and Bali; Supāśī, Vajrapāśā, Vajrapāṇi, and Mahābalā; Vajramālā, Mahāvidyā, and likewise Amṛtakuṇḍalī.

The great goddess Aparājitā, Kālakarṇī, and Mahābalā; likewise Dhanyā, the highly fortunate Padmakuṇḍalī, Puṣpadaṇḍī, Maṇicūḍā, Svanyakeśī, and Piṅgalā; the goddess Mahātejā, Dhanyā, and Vidyunmālinī;
the Rākṣasī Ekajaṭī, and the leaders of the Buddhas and Akṣitikās; and Kāpālinī.
The highly fortunate and blessed Āḍakeśvarī, as well as many other vidyās that bring benefit to sentient beings, such as: Kālikā, Rālikā, Kumbhāṇḍī, Śaṅkhinī, Kamalākṣī, Hārītī, Harikeśī,
Śrīmatī, Haripiṅgalā, Lambā, Pralambā, Kālapāśā, Kalaśodarī, Yamadūtī, and Yamarākṣasī.
O devourer of spirits! Accept this fragrance, flower, incense, lamp, and offering.

Be my protector and that of all sentient beings from all fears and calamities. May you behold a hundred assemblies and a hundred autumns. May the words of the mantra be efficacious, svāhā! This is the *pañcarakṣā* offering.

(33) Oṃ! Homage to the Blessed Prajñāpāramitā, the immeasurable one, the great yellow one, the great white one! You who hold in your hands the great blue jewel, a lotus, an elephant, and a book—enjoy this offering and the five nectars;
smell them! Oṃ picu picu! O increaser of wisdom! Blaze, blaze! O increaser of intelligence! Dhiri dhiri!

Svāhā to the increaser of intelligence! Oṃ, victory to the Śruti and Smṛti! Dhīḥ, svāhā to the one who is to be held in mind! This is the offering to Prajñāpāramitā. (34) Oṃ, you who uphold the earth, you who remove the fear of poverty and suffering! Oṃ dhīḥ, svāhā to the great victory of Śruti and Smṛti! O all you Yakṣiṇīs, come together quickly; [accept] this offering!
Take it, take it! Kha kha! Eat, eat! Oṃ dharaṇi dharaṇi svāhā! This is the *vasudhāra* offering.
(35) Oṃ, O gracious Tārā, whose mouth is nectar, whose eyes are nectar, who accomplishes all my aims, who brings joy to all sentient beings: take this offering, take it! Kha kha!
Eat, eat! Hūṃ phāṭ hrīṃ hrīṃ svāhā! This is the offering for Prasannatārā.
(36) Oṃ, homage to the one who neutralizes poison, the daughter of Śabari, the consumer of poison! Move! Strike together! O intoxicated elephant! O Avidhehe! Enjoy this offering; smell it! Oṃ jāḥ!
Jaḥ svāhā! The offering to Noble Aṅgulī.
(37) Oṃ, homage to the Blessed Lady Vajragāndhārī, she whose blazing splendor is ignited by many hundreds of thousands [of rays], she of fierce radiance, she who is terrifying! Come, come!

[O you who abide by the pledge] of the Three Jewels, including Satyananda and the others, and whoever else remains by their commitment: O Lord Abhūṣin, quickly accept this offering, accept it! [11] Oṃ mala mala | tulu tulu | mulu mulu | culu culu | dhama dhama | radga radga | radgapaya radgapaya | fulfill, fulfill my hope!
O Blessed One, Mahāvajragāndhārī! Siddhicaṇḍavajrapāṇi commands: svāhā!
This is the bali offering for Vajragāndhārī.
(38) Oṃ Dhvajāgrakeyūre! Victory, victory! Complete victory, complete victory!

O Jayāvahinī! Crush, crush all my enemies! Paralyze, paralyze! Grind, grind! Devour, devour! Hūṃ! Protect, protect me, O Blessed One! Accept, accept this offering! Shatter, shatter! For the destruction, for the destruction of the enemy army! Strike, strike the enemies, the enemies! Move, move!

Cili cili | tulu tulu | gala gala | kili kili | kulu kulu | *sarvatathāgatāvalokite svāhā* | *guṇarājaprābhāse svāhā* | *candrārkavimale svāhā* | *sarvanakṣatracamikariṇe svāhā* | *rakṣa rakṣa* | *sarvatathāgatebhyaḥ svāhā* | *dhvajāgrakeyūrabaliḥ*.

(39) Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, Uṣṇīṣavijayā! Destroy, destroy my death! Annihilate, annihilate! Cause to perish, cause to perish! Accept, accept this offering! Grant me long life and well-being, svāhā! This is the offering to Uṣṇīṣavijayā.

(40) Oṃ! To the Accomplished Solitary Hero, the Lord of Heroes, whose heart is tender with compassion, who holds a blue lotus in his hand: accept this offering, accept it! Eat it! Bestow peace! Accomplish all attainments! Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ! This is the offering to Siddhaikavīra.

Oṃ! To Yamāntaka, the terrifier of Yama; Hrīḥ Strīḥ! To the one with a distorted face, adorned with serpent ornaments, who holds a staff that crushes the three worlds in his hand, and who destroys the entire host of Māras—accept, accept this offering! Remove, remove my obstacles!
*Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā!* Ward off the four Māras! This is the *bali* offering for Yamāntaka.
*Oṃ vighnāntakamahākrodhamahābalaparākrama imaṃ baliṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa! Kha kha! Khāhi khāhi! Cut, cut all my obstacles!*
Bheda bheda! Drutaṃ! Daha daha! Paca paca! [12] Matha matha! Āḥ Vighnāntakṛta Hūṃ Svāhā! This is the *bali* offering for Vighnāntaka.
(43) Oṃ Bhagavati Grahamātṛke!

O Blessed One, Mother of the Planets, destroyer of the fear of all planets and constellations, pacifier of the fear of all gods, nāgas, yakṣas, and the like, eradicator of the fear of kings, thieves, and so forth—come quickly, come! Accept this offering, accept it! Remove all my obstacles.
Hara! Grant me peace, nourishment, and protection, hūṃ phaṭ svāhā! This is the bali offering for the planetary spirits.
(44) Oṃ, homage to the Lord of the World, whose lotus feet are worshipped by gods, asuras, humans, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and others.

To the Great Compassionate One, who is in a state of urgent haste to deliver all sentient beings from the hells without exception—accept, accept this *bali* offering together with milk and other ingredients! Deliver me and all sentient beings from the suffering of the hells and so forth;
deliver us! Lift us up! Lift us up! Raise us up completely! Raise us up completely! By the truth of the Buddha, by the truth of the Dharma...
By the truth of the Saṅgha, by the truth of this truthful speech: Oṃ Āḥ Hrīḥ Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā! This is the bali offering for all the Lords of the World.
(45) Oṃ, homage to the illustrious Khasarpaṇa, the mirror of the three worlds, whose mind is one-pointed; [homage] to him who swiftly pacifies all diseases, poverty, and suffering—this bali offering.

Having taken [the offering] together with milk and other substances, and having consumed it, perform for me peace, prosperity, and protection: *oṃ āḥ hrīḥ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. This is the *khasarpaṇa* bali.
(46) *Oṃ, homage to the Buddha, whose heart is filled with the burden of great compassion.*

To the one whose mind has arrived at the welfare of others, who possesses a single form throughout the three realms, and who performs great hardships for the sake of sentient beings—to you, this offering (bali) endowed with divine fragrance, color, and flavor is presented. Awaken all sentient beings and establish them in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment! Oṃ āḥ sugatavajratuṣṭya hoḥ hūṃ svāhā!
The Bali offering to the venerable Śrī Buddhahastaka:
(47) Oṃ, O remover of death and the five [mortalities], O dispeller of untimely death, O bringer of the end of poverty, suffering, and fear!

O remover of the eight great fears, O bestower of success through the sword, collyrium, sandals, and the auspicious jar; O Blessed Tārā, accept, accept this offering and the five nectars (pañcāmṛta)! Destroy, destroy my death! Oṃ tāre tuttāre ture svāhā! This is the offering for Nīlārā, the destroyer of the five deaths.
(48) Oṃ, homage to the Three Jewels!

Homage to Maṇibhadra, the great general of the yakṣas! Oṃ, to Ucchuṣma Jambhala, Lord of Waters! Accept this offering, accept it! Kha kha! Khāhi khāhi! Grant me great wealth! You are the giver! Svāhā!
The Offering to Ucchuṣma-Jambhala:
(49) Oṃ āḥ hrīṃ hūṃ! O Śuklaikajaṭī, accept this offering, accept it! Subdue all malevolent beings! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā! For the purpose of destroying the power of all Māras.
One should offer it. This is the white *ekajaṭī* offering:
(50) *Oṃ namaḥ kāyavākcittebhyaḥ*. To the serpent kings Karkoṭaka, Śaṅkhapāla, Ananta, Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Kulika, Padma, and Mahāpadma—this offering [is for you].
Accept, accept! [Accompanied by the suffering of various implements! Kha kha! Khāhi khāhi! Grant me accomplishment! Oṃ āḥ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā! This is the *nāgabali*.
(51) Oṃ, homage to the glorious Lord Maitreya!

To the Perfectly Awakened One who is endowed with the conduct of one who has realized future faults, whose mind is melted by compassion for the welfare of all beings: having partaken of this offering (*bali*) endowed with divine fragrance, color, and flavor, you shall establish me and all sentient beings out of the ocean of the suffering of *saṃsāra* in perfect awakening. Oṃ āḥ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. This is the *Maitreya-bali*.
(52) Oṃ indra-jama-jalaja-jakkha-bhūta-vahni-vāyu-rakkha-candra-sujjha-māda-vappatāli aṭṭhasāppa svāhā! Enjoy this offering; smell the flowers and incense; drink the ghee and the meat broth.

*Sādhakhāntikhuṇi-phaṭagāda hūṃ svāhā | Oṃ, the syllable A is the gateway to all phenomena because they are primordially unarisen; oṃ āḥ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā | This is the bali offering to Śrī Heruka. (53) Oṃ, Sahajasamvara, āḥ hūṃ! Come, come quickly!*
Take this offering, take it! Having eaten and become satisfied, having brought peace to all sentient beings, go, go to your own abodes, svāhā! This is the *śrīsahajasamvara-bali*.
(54) Oṃ tāre, remove everything for my sake, O wicked one!

Subdue, subdue all wicked beings! Delude, delude them! Grant me peace! O you who bring peace to all obstacles, in the primordial luminosity, accept, accept this offering and the five nectars! Kha kha! Eat, eat! Grant me nourishment! Grant me protection, defense, and concealment! Grant me all accomplishments!
Prayaccha hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ | Sarvaduṣṭapraduṣṭastambhanitāre svāhā | This is the bali offering for Noble Tārā. (55) Oṃ vajraghaṇṭe āḥ vajraghaṇṭe raṇi raṇi | praraṇa praraṇa |

*Saṃpraṇa saṃpraṇa! O you who traverse all buddha-fields, O Prajñāpāramitā, whose nature is sound, O heart of Vajrasattva, you who cause satisfaction: *hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā!* While ringing the bell for the purpose of reciting the True Dharma (*saddharma*), one should offer it with this mantra. [Likewise, one should offer] lamps, incense, perfumes, food offerings (*naivedya*), flowers, and betel.

And it should be taken according to the prescribed ritual. Then, with the words beginning "Thus the welfare of all sentient beings has been accomplished for you," one should dismiss them with the mantra: *oṃ vajramuḥ svāhā*. This is the *saddharmabali* (offering to the True Dharma).
*Oṃ*, all deities beginning with Brahmā, and those beginning with Indra, [listen] to me.

May the guardians—the nāgas, gandharvas, and yakṣas—be forever satisfied by this offering of strength. Oṃ, the syllable *a* is the gateway to all phenomena because they are primordially unarisen. Oṃ āḥ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā! This is the offering for all ritual activities.
Oṃ āḥ.

To Rāhu, Kāma, Agni, Candra, Sūrya, Maṅgala, Budha, Bṛhaspati, Śukra, Ketu, Śani, and the other wandering planets (care), as well as to the others—the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, and so forth—take this offering, take it!
Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā! This is the offering for all the grahas. [15]

Paca matha matha vidhvāṃsaya mahāsāhasrapramardanī! Gr̥hṇa gr̥hṇa imaṃ baliṃ!
Rakṣa rakṣa māṃ sarvasattvāṃś ca! Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā! This is the offering for Mahāsāhasrapramardanī.
(59) Oṃ mahāmāyūrīvidyārājñi, pacify all poisons for me!
Bring peace! Bring prosperity! Bring vision!

Strike down, strike down all calamities caused by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, and others! Burn, burn! Kill, kill! Roar, roar! Accept this offering, accept it! [Protect] me!

Protect, protect all sentient beings! Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā! This is the *Mahāmāyūrī-bali*. (60) Oṃ, Great Queen of Spells of the Cool Grove (*Mahāśītavana-vidyārājñī*), you who crush all that is evil: bring peace to me and to all sentient beings; bring nourishment; bring prosperity; [protect us] from *bhūtas*, *pretas*, *piśācas*, and the like!

Kill! Kill! Cause to kill! Cause to kill! Threaten! Threaten! Accept this *bali* offering! Accept it! Protect! Protect! Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā! This is the *bali* offering for Mahāśītavatī. (61) Oṃ Mahāpratisare, sovereign of all vidyās, accept this *bali*...
Seize, seize! Grant peace for me and for all sentient beings; grant nourishment, grant vision!
Slay, slay, crush the bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, and so forth! Protect, protect me and all sentient beings! Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā! This is the Mahāpratisarā bali offering.

(62) Oṃ mahāmantrānusāriṇi, destroyer of calamities! Accept this bali, accept it! Grant peace and nourishment for me and for all sentient beings! Protect us! Slay, slay all my enemies! Hrīṃ haḥ phaṭ svāhā! This is the bali offering for Mahāmantrānusāriṇī.
(63) This *Bali-mālikā*, the work of the venerable teacher Sumati-siṃha, is completed.
Homage to the Blessed One: O Siddhi, Siddhe, Mocani, Mokṣaṇī, Mukte, Amale, Vimale, Nirmale, Aṇḍare, Paṇḍare, Maṅgalam! O Golden Womb, you who are everywhere unimpeded, svāhā! [17]
